rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 3 "The handoff prompt that builds your kit": raw line 25 is the marker `{{prompt:agents-that-build-agents-handoff}}`; expanded (`node scripts/expand-md.js curriculum/lectures/agents-that-build-agents.md`, expanded line 25) it renders "**Prompt** *(Claude Code, same session, at the close after the stack scan)*" onto the slide. "The stack scan" is a never-named referent: it does not appear anywhere in this file's body (lines 1-56), and it never appears in ANY student-facing text in the module. It exists only in `curriculum/exercises/spot-gaps-build-the-loop.md`'s own maintainer block (lines 111, 113 — confirmed past that file's `<!-- maintainer -->` cut at line 95 via `grep -n "<!-- maintainer -->"`), where the exercise's own Phase 2 IS named for the student, but as "## Phase 2: Find the work you repeat across your stack" (line 49) — never as "the stack scan." A student reading this slide, in either layout, has no named beat to attach "the stack scan" to; the ONLY place that phrase exists in the whole training is internal authoring shorthand that leaked into the rendered prompt-block frontmatter (`curriculum/prompts/agents-that-build-agents-handoff.md` line 4: `context: same session, at the close after the stack scan`). Not a page-geometry issue (rule 12) — "after X" is a legitimate reading-order pointer — the noun X itself never resolves. Harm is real and concrete: this is the timing cue for when to run the capstone handoff prompt, and it fails to land for exactly the reader it addresses.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5 of 6 body headers are claim-shaped ("The move widens to everything you do", "The agent stops where your judgement begins", "The handoff prompt that builds your kit", "You make agentic happen", "There is no last turn"). Chunk 5's header "Ralph" is a bare proper-noun label — the rule's own NOT-violations list names this exact case verbatim: "catalogue entries naming their subject (*Ralph*, *The numbers*, *Verification, named*)". Closest-to-violating header, and the compendium settles it directly rather than by house-convention inference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 9 body bullets (chunk 4 x3, chunk 5 x4, chunk 6 x2) against the three classes. Closest-to-violating: chunk 6 line 52's anaphora-triple close ("Each move makes the next session cheaper") echoes chunk 1 line 7's "Every packaged move makes the next session cheaper" near-verbatim — a candidate (a) doctrine restatement. Kept as PASS: this is the training's dead-last beat (per maintainer Placement block, `agents-that-build-agents` is the final lecture of the final module), and the echo is the deliberate full-circle closing device (session -> gap -> move -> cheaper session, looping back to "session") rather than a meta-announcement of a lens already used — rule 2's own text grants closers latitude to sum the whole deck ("a closer summing the whole deck is a closer doing its job"), and cutting the echo would break a deliberate repetition per the dispatch preamble's own carve-out. "Practitioners see levers first." (chunk 5 line 46, trimmed by the 2026-08-25 lean pass) is the generalizing moral the anecdote earns, not a (c) aphorism kicker restating the header "Ralph" or a `**The point:**` line — it introduces the priority (notice available levers) the preceding three bullets illustrate but never state outright. No (b) self-referential design commentary found: "This one closes the module" (chunk 3 line 23) and "Agents that build agents is a collaboration in the same shape as everything else here" (chunk 2 line 15) are substantive orientation/consolidation claims about the subject matter and the module's structure, not the curriculum narrating its own pedagogical design.
